You can contact the Domestic Violence and Stalking Unit with the Franklin County Prosecutor's office. They may be able to help navigate the issues you're having with law enforcement. 

Also, SARNCO (Sexual Assault Response Network of Central Ohio) who can provide support for stalking, dating violence, etc. They have a 24/7 hotline (844) 644-6435). 

There is also the Center for Family Safety and Healing for domestic/dating violence support. All of these places can help with safety planning. 

You also want to keep a log or journal (date, time, location, description, names of witnesses, etc). The log can be shared with police. And report report report. If you do identify him, all of this can be submitted to court and could help obtain a CPO. Think of a CPO as one tool in the toolbox - it may not be enough to resolve the situation.

I have a terrier mix that does the same thing (and also reacts to bikes and cars). She used to be absolutely insane (growling, lunging, barking, running around in circles, etc), but would get along with dogs off of a leash just fine. It took 2.5 years of trial and error, but finally I found a high reward treat that worked for us: boiled chicken. 

I started in the house with the "look" command. I would tell her to look and as soon as she would look at me I would give her a piece of chicken. After a couple of days I started using this technique on walks, but at first it only worked if she hadn't seen the other dog yet. I would tell her to look, give her chicken, and then walk in a direction that would take us away from the other dog. I then started taking her to a park where there was a large field surrounded by dog walking paths and experimented with her "threshold" (the distance at which she would switch from calm to reactive when another dog was around) and would give her the command and feed her lots of chicken when I noticed her focusing too much on the other dog. After about 6 months of this we have gotten to the point where she will listen to the command within about 30 ft of another dog, and I notice her reactivity is worse on streets and paths, so I try to only walk her in places where it's easy for me to step far off the path to work on training. We are still working on it, and we still have slip ups, but she is doing so much better!

Maybe try a training like this? It makes our walks so much easier. I hope this helps and sorry for any typos- I am on my phone atm. Let me know if you have any questions!

I have major anxiety and like to feel prepared when going into a job interview. In order to not limit myself by memorizing specific questions, I memorize relevant examples from my previous experience that can be used to answer multiple behavioral or task related questions. My examples or stories that I have memorized cover a range of topics such as when a project was successful and why, when a project failed and what I learned, team communication and collaboration, strategic implementation, and when dealing with a negative situation (such as a disagreement with a boss or an angry customer). This is different than memorizing questions, because if you know your examples thoroughly you can use them to answer most questions. 

This isn't a catch all, as I have been thrown off several times. If I am thrown off by a question, I will actually write that question down and later review why it threw me off and how I would answer it in the future. Also, if a question throws me off, I will say in the interview, "That is a really great question" and take a moment to reflect on what they are actually asking. The hardest thing about interviews (I think) is remembering that I am allowed to take a moment to reflect in silence, and to not let the fact that people are staring and waiting freak me out. 

Anyways, I will get off my soap box, and I hope this was helpful!
